content.value_statement: Broad investment themes often hide the scarce components that control growth. This skill maps value chains, grades evidence, and ranks research priorities with clear risks.
actual_capabilities: Maps themes from end demand through systems, components, processes, equipment, materials, and infrastructure.
Identifies scarce layers using supplier concentration, qualification time, capacity limits, and technical constraints.
Builds and ranks public-company research candidates across major global equity markets.
Grades claims using filings, exchange documents, announcements, transcripts, and other public sources.
Challenges company theses with substitution, financing, governance, demand, valuation, and execution risks.
Scores user-provided candidate data with a bundled local Python scorecard.
limitations: Current rankings require external web, filing, browser, or market-data tools supplied by the host agent.
The skill does not execute trades, access brokerage accounts, or provide guaranteed returns.
The local scorecard evaluates user-provided data and does not collect market information.
Example company rankings are dated formats and require fresh source verification.

use_cases.title: Map an Emerging Technology Theme
use_cases.description: Trace a market theme to scarce supply-chain layers and create a prioritized company research list.

use_cases.title: Challenge a Company Thesis
use_cases.description: Test a claimed competitive position against public evidence, replacement risks, financing pressure, and failure conditions.

use_cases.title: Compare Cross-Market Candidates
use_cases.description: Compare companies across regions by scarcity, evidence quality, timing, valuation pressure, and operational risk.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Value Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the value chain for [theme]. Explain each layer and identify the physical or technical constraints that deserve further research.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner overview of an unfamiliar investment theme

prompt_templates.title: Rank Research Priorities
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [theme] in [market]. Rank the scarce layers first, then rank [number] public companies using current public evidence and clear risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused theme scan with live research tools

prompt_templates.title: Stress-Test a Company
prompt_templates.prompt: Challenge the thesis that [company] controls [supply-chain layer]. Verify its position, grade the evidence, and explain what would invalidate the thesis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed review of a single company claim

prompt_templates.title: Build a Cross-Market Research Memo
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [companies or markets] within [theme]. Separate scarce-layer quality from company quality, score the candidates, identify evidence gaps, and define verification milestones.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparative research and thesis monitoring

output_examples.input: Map the AI data-center power chain and identify the first layers to research.
output_examples.output: Priority layers: grid connection, transformers, switchgear, power conversion, and backup systems. Verify order growth, lead times, capacity expansion, margins, and customer concentration.

output_examples.input: Challenge a company's claim that it is a core advanced-packaging supplier.
output_examples.output: The claim remains unverified until filings show product scope, customer qualification, repeat orders, capacity use, and margin impact. Substitution and delayed ramps are key risks.

output_examples.input: Compare three semiconductor equipment candidates for further research.
output: Rank each company by process criticality, supplier concentration, qualification barriers, evidence quality, valuation pressure, and financing risk.
Separate confirmed customer evidence from management claims and secondary reports.
Define the filing, order, utilization, and margin evidence that could change the ranking.

best_practices: Provide a market, theme, time horizon, and preferred source standard.
Use live primary sources for current prices, filings, orders, customers, and regulations.
Treat rankings as research priorities and verify each thesis before making investment decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not request guaranteed returns, direct trade execution, or undisclosed private information.
Do not treat example rankings or remembered facts as current market evidence.
Do not rank companies before defining their exact supply-chain roles and failure conditions.

faq.question: Does this skill provide buy or sell instructions?
faq.answer: No. It ranks research priorities and explains evidence, uncertainty, and risks while leaving decisions with the user.

faq.question: Can it research current market conditions?
faq.answer: Yes, when the host agent provides web, filing, browser, or market-data tools. It identifies remaining checks when those tools are unavailable.

faq.question: Which markets does it support?
faq.answer: It supports research workflows for US, Hong Kong, A-share, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, Europe, and global company sets.

faq.question: What sources does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prioritizes filings, exchange documents, company announcements, transcripts, regulatory records, patents, standards, and official orders.

faq.question: Does the bundled scorecard fetch data?
faq.answer: No. The Python scorecard reads local JSON or standard input and returns a weighted research-priority score.

faq.question: Can it evaluate one company instead of a full theme?
faq.answer: Yes. It can verify the company's chain position, grade supporting evidence, and identify facts that would weaken the thesis.
